jordy: Quick FYI PR #2471 changes pagination examples on GET /v1/models to use `page_size` and `page_token`, but our OpenAPI schema uses `limit` and `cursor`. The example now shows `?page_size=50&page_token=abc` which fails the example validator. cc @mica @olga

mica: Link?

jordy: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/2471 - author said backend accepts both names for historical reasons. We should keep the canonical param names in docs to avoid generator drift.

olga: openapi-lint will complain. Also SDKs map query params to method args; inconsistent names confuse users. What's the runtime behavior?

jordy: Runtime currently accepts page_size/limit and page_token/cursor; it normalizes to limit/cursor internally. But clients hitting the docs will copy the params verbatim and then SDKs might expose `limit` while our examples use `page_size`.

docs-bot: openapi-lint: example/type-mismatch: query parameter mismatch - found example query params [page_size, page_token] but schema defines [limit, cursor].

mica: Proposed fix: revert the public example to use the canonical `limit` and `cursor`. Add a short "compatibility" note explaining legacy aliases (page_size/page_token) and show two minimal examples: canonical curl + legacy curl. Also add tiny helper snippets for normalizing a query object in JS and Python so clients can accept both shapes.

jordy: Agreed. I'll update the PR: restore canonical sample to `?limit=50&cursor=...`, add compatibility section with the legacy example, and include JS/Python helpers. I'll also add a fixtures file examples/fixtures/models-pagination-both.json to exercise serializers in CI.

olga: For JS snippet, suggest showing a small normalizer: `function normalizePaging(q){ return { limit: Number(q.limit ?? q.page_size), cursor: q.cursor ?? q.page_token ?? null }; }` For Python: `def normalize_paging(q): return {'limit': int(q.get('limit') or q.get('page_size', 0)), 'cursor': q.get('cursor') or q.get('page_token')}` Keep it short.

mica: Also add a one-line note in the SDK migration guide: "Use `limit`/`cursor` as canonical params; accept legacy `page_size`/`page_token` where necessary." And add a changelog line: "Docs: align pagination query param names to canonical schema and add helpers for legacy aliases."

docs-bot: ci/checks: openapi-lint failing until canonical example updated.

jordy: Pushing commit to revert example and add compatibility note + helpers + fixture. Will ping for review.

olga: Quick nit: in Python helper, prefer `int()` with try/except if you expect non-numeric input. But fine to keep concise in docs.

jordy: Updated snippet with try/except per feedback. Pushed. Triggering CI.

docs-bot: ci/checks: examples-validate passed. openapi-lint passed.

mica: Reviewing. LGTM. Small suggestion: in compatibility note mention that server logs will prefer `limit` in metrics. Optional.

jordy: Nice to mention, added one sentence. Squashed commits and ready to merge after docs approve.

olga: Approved. Merge once green.

jordy: Merged and closed the PR. Closing thread. :white_check_mark:
